Hi Tessa,

Thanks for sending the MSA and order form. Our legal team did an initial pass and flagged the indemnity section — specifically the third-party IP claim language and the defense-control allocation. We attached our redlines (BL_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx) and a short summary of our positions. High-level concerns: 

- Brightline needs control of defense for third-party IP claims that allege infringement of our use of the service; we are uncomfortable with the vendor having unilateral control.
- We need clarity on whether AI-generated outputs are covered, and carve-outs for customer-provided content.
- We also want a mutual indemnity for third-party claims related to data we bring to the platform.

Can we schedule a short call this week to walk through the redlines and try to narrow issues? Prefer Wed/Thu morning PST. If possible please include whoever owns legal at Redwood.

Subject: Internal: proposed positions on Brightline redlines (indemnity)

Tessa / Ben — following Samantha's redlines, below are Redwood's recommended positions and fallback compromises I can sign off on. I put the prioritized items first.

1) Defense control (third-party IP claims) — Redwood position: vendor-led defense with right for customer to participate and reasonable consent over settlements that impose equitable relief or ongoing obligations.
   - Rationale: Vendor needs control to coordinate technical defense, avoid inconsistent defenses across customers, and manage insurance coverage.
   - Customer ask (full customer control) risks duplicative counsel and inconsistent technical positions.
   - Compromise language we can offer: vendor shall have the right to assume and control the defense of any third-party IP claim provided that Vendor (a) gives Customer prompt notice, (b) allows Customer to participate with counsel of its choice at its own expense, and (c) does not settle any claim that would (i) impose an ongoing obligation on Customer or (ii) materially adversely affect Customer without Customer's prior written consent (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld).

2) AI-generated outputs — Redwood position: indemnity applies only for claims that arise from Vendor's use of non-customer-provided training data or willful infringement by Vendor; not for outputs driven solely by customer prompts.
   - Compromise: carve out Customer-provided content (including prompts and datasets) from Vendor indemnity; for generated outputs, offer narrow indemnity tied to documented reproduction of a third-party work in Vendor's model training or fine-tune corpus.

3) Mutual indemnity for Customer data — Redwood willing to include limited mutual indemnity for claims arising from Customer-supplied data/content (e.g., if customer provides infringing content). Keep standard caps and process for notice/cooperation.

4) Caps and insurance — propose to keep monetary cap at order form level (e.g., 1x annual committed spend) and offer to provide certificate of insurance on request. If customer requires higher cap, push to procurement/sales to agree commercial offset.

5) Evidence & triage — recommend we ask Brightline to produce evidence of alleged infringement and allow Redwood a reasonable time to investigate before any admission or settlement.

I can draft redline language for the call. If Ben / Logan want me to soften any of the items for commercial reasons, tell me which point to prioritize (defense control vs cap vs AI-output carve-out).

—Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Redlines to MSA / Order Form — indemnity concerns

Kimberly / Tessa — thanks for the quick reply and proposed compromise language. A few points from Brightline / Harper Legal's side: 

- Brightline cannot accept a vendor-only defense for third-party IP claims that relate to our use of the service. Our concern is primarily equitable relief and reputational damage — we need to be able to control the overall defense strategy.
- We are open to vendor conducting the initial technical response, but require that Brightline have the right to assume defense within 10 days if it reasonably believes Vendor's defense is inadequate (common carve).
- On AI outputs: Brightline's ask is that Redwood indemnify for third-party IP claims arising from outputs that reproduce a third party's copyrighted material when that reproduction occurs as a direct result of Vendor's model (i.e., not when Customer supplies the copyrighted content in a prompt). We are flexible on requiring Brightline to provide evidence of reproduction.

Suggested compromise language (drafted for call):
- For third-party IP claims, the parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to coordinate defense. Vendor may manage the technical discovery and initial response. However, Customer may assume control of the defense (including choice of counsel) upon written notice within 10 calendar days after Vendor assumes control; Vendor shall not settle without Customer's prior written consent if settlement would impose ongoing obligations on Customer.

- For outputs, replace broad carve with: Vendor will indemnify Customer for claims that a reproduced expressive work in Vendor-generated output is infringing where Customer can demonstrate (i) the output reproduces the third-party work, and (ii) the reproduction stems from Vendor's training corpus rather than Customer-submitted content.

We believe this language appropriately balances operational needs with Brightline's governance requirements. Happy to discuss on Wed/Thu — we prefer Wed morning.

Regards,
Julia Lawson
Partner, Harper Legal (outside counsel for Brightline)

Team — thanks for the productive back-and-forth. Quick summary and recommended next steps so we can close this item in the term sheet: 

Summary of proposed middle-ground:
- Defense control: Redwood will assume initial defense for third-party IP claims; Brightline may assume control within 10 days upon written notice if it reasonably believes Redwood's defense is inadequate. Redwood will not settle any claim that imposes ongoing obligations on Brightline without Brightline's consent.
- AI outputs: Redwood to indemnify where Customer can demonstrate that the infringing reproduction is attributable to Vendor's training corpus (not customer-submitted content). We will require basic evidence (sample output + comparison).
- Mutual data indemnity: include limited mutual indemnity for claims arising from customer-supplied content; standard cooperation/notice clauses to apply.
- Caps & insurance: keep the proposed order-form cap (1x committed annual spend) by default; if Brightline needs a higher cap we will table that as a commercial exception to be handled by Logistics/Commercial (Logan).

Action items:
1) Kimberly to produce redline with the exact compromise language (I give the green light to include the 10-day assume-defense carve and AI-output clause as drafted by Julia) — Kimberly, can you circulate by EOD Mon?
2) Samantha / Julia to review the redline; if acceptable we can fold into the order form and move to signature.
3) Logan / Ben to confirm whether the customer requires higher cap; if so we will return with commercial offset options.

Samantha — can you confirm Wed 9:00 PST for a 30-min call to iron out any final edits? If yes we will send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Tessa
